why: rcl keeps a thread-local error state with a formatted message, file and line, read back with rcl_get_error_string(). nano-ros returns `rcl_ret_t` and nothing else -- there is no nros_error_string() and no per-thread error slot. What a C user loses is real and should be said plainly: a code, never a message. The constraint is thread-local storage plus a formatted-string buffer per thread, on targets where a task stack is measured in kilobytes.
